jobs.title: Supply Chain Manager, Strategic Engagement Partnerships, Global Procurement Sustainability, GPO
jobs.description:
Amazon’s Global Procurement Sustainability (GPS) team is transforming procurement into a catalyst for global impact, advancing environmental stewardship, economic opportunity, human rights, and community resilience through purpose-driven sourcing.
GPS connects Amazon’s purchasing power to purpose across four strategic pillars: Supplier Development & Impact (SDI), Community Impact (CI), Social Responsibility & Human Rights (SR), and Environment (ENV).
We are seeking a leader to architect and lead GPS’s external engagement strategy at scale. This is a highly visible, executive-facing role for a leader who can translate vision into influence, building partnerships, shaping policy, storytelling, and positioning procurement as a lever for systemic change.
You will serve as the connective force across all four GPS pillars, designing integrated engagement strategies that amplify impact across suppliers, governments, industry alliances, and global stakeholders. This role blends strategy, diplomacy, and execution requiring both executive presence and operational rigor.

Key job responsibilities
Key Responsibilities

Spearhead or contributethe design and execution of a global engagement strategy that advances responsible procurement priorities across Amazon’s Global Procurement Organization. Establish governance, communication, and reporting frameworks that enable alignment, scalability, and measurable impact.

Develop and drive a comprehensive external impact and recognition strategy across Supplier Development & Impact, Community Impact, Social Responsibility & Human Rights, and Environment. Translate data into compelling narratives, executive briefings, and stakeholder-facing outputs that elevate thought leadership and demonstrate measurable outcomes.

Build and manage strategic partnerships with governments, NGOs, corporate partners, academic institutions, and industry alliances. Structure collaborations that expand inclusive supplier ecosystems, strengthen human rights practices, and accelerate environmental sustainability goals.

Serve as a key liaison to Government Affairs and public sector stakeholders, influencing policy initiatives related to economic inclusion, responsible sourcing, and sustainable procurement standards.

Design and lead multi-stakeholder activations—including supplier summits, policy roundtables, and industry forums—ensuring seamless execution and clear impact measurement.

Drive cross-functional alignment across GPS pillars and internal teams, ensuring consistent external messaging, streamlined supplier engagement, and integrated delivery of global sustainability objectives.

A day in the life
You start your day reviewing partnership performance metrics and preparing for an internal session designed to align partnership strategy to multiple pillars need simultaneously. Mid-morning, you collaborate with industry partners to design an initiative that advances responsible procurement goals. After lunch, you brief leadership on partnership impact internally and externally and recognition progress. Your afternoon includes coordinating stakeholder participation for a global summit, reviewing event performance insights, and refining messaging for an industry keynote. Throughout the day, you balance strategy and execution, connecting stakeholders, advancing partnerships, and driving measurable impact across GPS and GPO priorities.

About the team
GPS is part of Amazon’s Global Procurement Organization (GPO), working to make everyday purchasing decisions a force for good. Our mission is to accelerate positive outcomes for people and the planet through purpose-led procurement.
The Strategic Engagement & Partnerships function sits at the heart of GPS’s external presence, connecting our four pillars to a global ecosystem of stakeholders. Together, we influence thousands of procurement professionals and suppliers across multiple countries, embedding sustainability into every sourcing decision.

jobs.title: Content & Partnerships Manager, Amazon Music
jobs.description:
Amazon Music Japan is looking for a Content & Partnerships Manager to join our team in Tokyo.

Amazon Music Japan's original content strategy is built around a clear customer loop: fans discover Amazon Music content through Prime Video and Fire TV, engage with the content, and convert into active music streamers through integrated in-content experiences. This role sits at the center of that loop — ensuring productions are delivered on time, content reaches customers across the right surfaces, and partners are managed with rigor.

This is a high-ownership execution role spanning original content and live-streaming production, Prime Video and Fire TV coordination, and sponsorship operations. You will manage external production partners and agencies, coordinate with Prime Video and Fire TV teams on content delivery and surface integration, support sponsorship activation and fulfillment, and work closely with internal stakeholders across Global Content, Marketing, Artist Relations, Business Affairs, and Legal to bring productions to market on time and on budget.

The right candidate brings production project management experience, strong operational instincts, and the ability to work fluidly across Japanese and English-speaking stakeholders at all levels.

Key job responsibilities
Content Production
- Own end-to-end project management of content productions from brief through delivery: manage timelines, vendors, budgets, and cross-functional deliverables across internal teams and external partners
- Manage artist booking logistics and production coordination with external production companies, in coordination with the internal Artist Relations and Label Relations teams.
- Coordinate with Prime Video and Fire TV teams on content delivery schedules, asset requirements, and surface integration — ensuring productions are technically and operationally ready for launch across all O&O endpoints
- Partner with Global Content, Artist Relations, Label Relations, and Legal/Business Affairs to ensure content agreements are in place, production milestones are tracked, and stakeholder alignment is maintained throughout production
- Coordinate cross-functionally with Marketing, Social, PR, and Product to ensure content launches are supported by integrated go-to-market plans
Sponsorship Operations & Partner Management
- Support sponsorship execution for designated Amazon Music Japan properties: manage partner deliverables, asset collection, activation coordination, and post-campaign reporting
- Coordinate with Amazon Ads stakeholders on sponsorship fulfillment and integrated media execution
- Support development of sponsorship materials and post-campaign reports in partnership with senior team members and global revenue teams

Performance & Planning
- Track and report on production and commercial performance; identify risks early and escalate with proposed solutions
- Connect content performance metrics - views, unique customers - to downstream Amazon Music growth outcomes including music first streams to evaluate production effectiveness
- Manage vendor and agency relationships: scope work, negotiate terms, and hold partners accountable to quality and delivery standards
- Contribute to annual content and partnership planning, including budget forecasting and post-mortem learnings

A day in the life
No two days look the same, but most involve moving between production detail and business context in the same hour.
You might start by reviewing a delivery schedule with a production company, then shift to resolving a platform spec issue with an internal team.

Midday could be unblocking a talent booking with Artist Relations, or preparing a sponsor deliverables tracker for a media agency.

In the afternoon, flagging a performance risk before it becomes a miss — then scoping a new production with a vendor. Throughout, you hold the operational picture across workstreams, in both Japanese and English, so nothing slips.

About the team
Amazon Music is an immersive audio entertainment service that deepens connections between fans, artists, and creators. From personalized music playlists to exclusive podcasts, concert livestreams to artist merch, Amazon Music is innovating at some of the most exciting intersections of music and culture. We offer experiences that serve all listeners with our different tiers of service: Prime members get access to all the music in shuffle mode, and top ad-free podcasts, included with their membership; customers can upgrade to Amazon Music Unlimited for unlimited, on-demand access to 100 million songs, including millions in HD, Ultra HD, and spatial audio; and anyone can listen for free by downloading the Amazon Music app or via Alexa-enabled devices. Join us for the opportunity to influence how Amazon Music engages fans, artists, and creators on a global scale.
Basic qualifications:
- 4+ years of program or project management experience
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English, and have the ability to take direction in English
- Speak, write, and read fluently in Japanese
- Experience working in content production, live entertainment, or a related field, including rights clearance and talent/vendor coordination
- Proven ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder projects from planning through delivery
- Experience managing external vendors, agencies, or production partners
- Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, manage multiple workstreams simultaneously, and make sound judgment calls under ambiguity
Preferred qualifications:
- Experience in music, entertainment, or media — particularly live events, festivals, original video series, or streaming platforms
- Familiarity with streaming platform operations, including content delivery and distribution workflows
- Experience supporting sponsorship activation and fulfillment, including working with brand advertisers and media agencies
- Familiarity with Japanese entertainment industry stakeholders: music agencies, talent management, broadcast and streaming platforms, brand advertisers, and media agencies
- Experience working in a global organization with distributed teams across multiple time zones

jobs.description:
Amazon's Global Law Enforcement Engagement (LEE) function within the Security Operations Group (SOG) is seeking a member to execute and deliver against the LEE operating model across assigned markets and workstreams. This is a new role within a newly formed function.

You will contribute to building Amazon's institutional law enforcement relationship capability — populating the LE Partnership Registry, executing engagement playbooks, maintaining relationship records, and supporting the speed-of-response SLAs that underpin LEE's service to field S&LP, Investigations, and Regional Security teams. You will work within developing frameworks and governance structures, applying subject-matter expertise in law enforcement engagement to deliver consistent, compliant, and measurable outcomes.

At this level, you are expected to operate autonomously within defined scope: executing engagement plans, resolving operational friction with law enforcement contacts, maintaining data integrity across the registry, and escalating appropriately when issues exceed your remit. You will use your law enforcement or security background to serve as a credible point of contact for agencies in assigned jurisdictions, support the drafting of playbooks and MoU documentation, and contribute intelligence inputs that strengthen Amazon's proactive security posture.

You will work across multiple jurisdictions with different legal and cultural frameworks, requiring sound judgement, attention to regulatory compliance, and the ability to coordinate with internal stakeholders (Legal, GSOC, Investigations, field S&LP) to deliver outcomes. You are not expected to design the architecture — you are expected to execute it with precision, identify improvement opportunities, and raise the bar on quality and consistency within your assigned scope.

Key job responsibilities
Build and maintain law enforcement relationships at regional and local levels within assigned jurisdictions — recording all contacts, engagement activity, and status updates in the LE Partnership Registry to ensure institutional ownership.
Execute standardised engagement playbooks by jurisdiction and scenario, identifying improvement opportunities.
Operate within the information-sharing authorization-tier matrix, coordinating with Legal to ensure all data exchanges within assigned scope meet GDPR and local regulatory requirements.

Contribute intelligence inputs (threat briefings, advisories, incident data) to internal teams, supporting LEE's shift from reactive to preventative.
Support MoU delivery with priority law enforcement agencies; coordinate and deliver joint training sessions, tabletop exercises, and community engagement events within assigned markets.
Coordinate with internal customers (field S&LP, Investigations, GSOC, R&R, Legal) to resolve operational friction, maintain service accessibility, and support cross-pillar referrals across SOG and partner teams.
Maintain data quality and reporting accuracy across assigned WBR metrics, escalating deviations and identifying process improvement opportunities

About the team
The Law Enforcement Engagement team sits within Amazon's Security Operations Group, building the institutional architecture that connects Amazon's security operations with law enforcement agencies across 30+ international markets to disrupt organised crime targeting global logistics.

We believe relationships built in peacetime pay dividends in crisis. We deploy resources where data shows the greatest exposure, measure ourselves on outcomes — disrupted Mo's, asset recovery, threat disruption — not activity.

This is a team for builders. We are early-stage, high-ambition, and outcome-obsessed. You'll write the playbook, not inherit one.
Basic qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Knowledge of Microsoft Office products and applications at an advanced level
- Experience working with global cross-functional teams
- Experience in security service, loss prevention, asset protection, audit, investigations, law enforcement, risk management, data analytics, inventory control, quality assurance or a related field
- Experience working cross-functionally and across regions
- Experience creating and delivering written and oral communications for technical and non-technical audiences
- Deep experience with public-private partnerships and information-sharing programmes across multiple jurisdictions
Preferred qualifications:
- Master's degree in relevant field

jobs.title: Talent & Partnerships Lead, XCM - Cross-Category, Cross-Channel Marketing
jobs.description:
We're looking for a Talent & Partnerships Lead to join the XCM Creative Production team. This person will own the day-to-day sourcing, vetting, and engagement of celebrity and creator talent across Amazon's global brand campaigns. They'll serve as the connective tissue between XCM's Big Rock creative vision and the agency and management ecosystem that represents top-tier talent, ensuring the right names surface at the right time for the right briefs. Beyond individual deals, this role shapes XCM's broader talent strategy: building a forward-looking pipeline, tracking cultural relevance, maintaining agency relationships, and advising creative leadership on where to place bets.

Key job responsibilities
**Talent Sourcing & Pipeline**

- Build and maintain a continuously updated talent pipeline spanning actors, musicians, athletes, creators, and cultural figures across categories and markets.

- Proactively surface talent options for upcoming campaigns, matching creative intent, audience alignment, brand safety, and budget parameters.

- Track cultural moments, emerging creators, and shifting audience affinities to keep recommendations current.

**Agency & Management Relationships**

- Serve as XCM's primary point of contact with major talent agencies (CAA, WME, UTA, ICM) and independent management firms.

- Cultivate relationships that give the team early access to talent availability windows, deal structures, and scheduling constraints.

- Negotiate initial deal terms and coordinate with Business Affairs on contract execution.

**Big Rock Alignment**

- Partner with Big Rock creative leads and producers to translate campaign briefs into talent profiles and shortlists.

- Participate in early creative development to flag casting feasibility, timing conflicts, and budget trade-offs before concepts lock.

- Ensure talent selections ladder up to XCM's annual tentpole calendar and cross-campaign strategy.

**Talent Strategy**

- Develop and maintain XCM's talent strategy framework: who we pursue, why, and how we sequence investments across the portfolio.

- Advise leadership on category gaps, competitive landscape (who competitors are signing), and long-term partnership opportunities vs. one-off bookings.

- Own post-campaign talent performance analysis. Track social lift, earned media, brand perception shifts, and audience resonance to inform future casting.

**Cross-Functional Coordination**

- Collaborate with Legal, Business Affairs, and Brand Safety on vetting, contracting, and risk assessment.

A day in the life
You start the morning scanning overnight agency submissions, a handful of availability checks you sent yesterday now have answers. One A-list name opened up for the Q4 window, another passed. You update the talent tracker and flag the opening to the Big Rock lead before their 10am creative review.

Mid-morning, you're on a call with a UTA agent walking through their client roster for a Spring sports campaign. You're listening for schedule flexibility and deal appetite as much as star power. You take notes on two athletes worth a deeper conversation and schedule follow-ups.

Before lunch, you join the weekly Big Rock sync. The team is debating two creative directions for a Holiday tentpole. You pull up comps, share recent social engagement data on the talent in question, and flag a timing conflict with one candidate's press tour. The room shifts direction based on what you surface.

After lunch, you're building a shortlist deck for a new brief that just landed. You pull from your pipeline, cross-reference budget thresholds with Business Affairs, and write up a point of view on each name: why them, what's the risk, what's the negotiation leverage.

Late afternoon, you hop on a quick sync with the XCM production team about an upcoming shoot. Talent's team has a rider question and a scheduling wrinkle. You broker a solution that keeps the shoot date intact without blowing the line item.

About the team
XCM’s Creative team is the internal marketing team setting design and brand direction for Amazon’s global brand. Our mission is to be the most customer-centric collective of creative thinkers, dreamers and doers. This manifest itself through visual design, branding, photography, video, social, digital, advertising and user experience design. We are responsible for branding and the creative development of style guides for the Amazon master brand and collaborate with business partners around the world to support a wide range of devices, services, features, and retail categories. We apply strategic insight to delight customers -driving discovery, engagement, and trust. We’re growing quickly and hiring the best. This is day one.
Basic qualifications:
- 5+ years of digital content management, communications, or content strategy experience
Preferred qualifications:
- 3+ years of entertainment, brand or production entity experience

jobs.title: Fleet Data Manager (Fixed-term contract), Amazon's Fleet Procurement and Capacity Planning
jobs.description:
Amazon's Fleet Procurement and Capacity Planning (FPAC) team manages a large-scale international commercial vehicle fleet across 10 European markets. This fleet depends on accurate, timely data flowing between two Fleet Management Companies (FMCs), Amazon's internal planning systems, and multiple cross-functional stakeholders.

This role owns the operational delivery and quality of all fleet data provided by FMCs (Ayvens and Arval) to Amazon. You will be the single-threaded owner ensuring that vehicle lifecycle data (from order placement through deployment, maintenance, defleeting, and remarketing) is delivered per contractual SLAs, meets validation standards, and flows reliably into the planning tools and reporting mechanisms that drive fleet capacity decisions.

This is a hands-on data operations and vendor management role. You will spend the majority of your time ensuring data reliability, resolving reporting failures with FMC technical contacts, and supporting the internal teams who depend on this data to make procurement and capacity decisions worth hundreds of millions in OPEX annually.

Please note that this is a 12 months fixed-term contract.

Key job responsibilities
1- Maintain Fleet Data Reliability
- Own the end-to-end data delivery relationship with Ayvens and Arval technical points of contact, ensuring reporting against established SLAs and contractual obligations
- Monitor, triage, and resolve data quality issues across SDR (Supply Delivery Reporting) and SRR (Supply Return Reporting) pipelines, including idle stock positions at VIN level
- Support Weekly Business Reviews and Variable Last Mile Rentals reporting cadences by ensuring upstream data is accurate and delivered on time
- Escalate systemic data failures through the appropriate FMC governance channels (Monthly Business Reviews, performance reviews).
2- Enable Planning Tools and Downstream Consumers
- Ensure data feeds into FORCE (Fleet Optimization, Requirement and Control Engine) and FAB (Fleet Allocation and Balancing) meet signal integration requirements
- Partner with the MAPS team (Mid-Term Planning) and Fleet Planning to resolve data gaps that block planning accuracy and automation
- Triage new data requests from internal stakeholders against existing data specifications; eliminate redundancy before placing additional requirements on FMCs
3- Drive Continuous Improvement

- Identify and implement process improvements to reduce manual data reconciliation effort
- Develop monitoring mechanisms to proactively flag reporting inaccuracies before they propagate into planning decisions
- Document and maintain the fleet data catalogue, including ownership, refresh cadences, quality thresholds, and known limitations
- Ensure any new fleet programs (LMR expansion, new country launches, Middle Mile integration) include data requirements in vendor agreements from the outset
4- Cross-Functional Coordination

- Align with Fleet Partnerships (FMC contractual owners), Fleet Deployment & Redeployment, Planning, and GFPA (Global Fleet Planning Analytics) on data priorities and dependencies
- Influence FMC behavior through performance metrics and contractual accountability rather than direct authority
- Represent data requirements in FMC governance forums (MBR/QBR)

A day in the life
Basic qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Experience working with data analytics and using these metrics to identify problems, or experience in an operational role
- Experience in vendor management, or experience in operations and on-call support for data center facilities, mission critical plants, or production facilities
- Experience performing data analysis and troubleshooting data integrity issues
Preferred qualifications:
- Experience in transportation or supply chain within a high-volume logistics, manufacturing or engineering environment
- Experience working within a global company, with multi-country responsibilities
- Experience in procurement, supply chain, inventory management, contract management, lease administration or operations
- Experience managing data pipelines
- Experience with machine learning/statistical modeling data analysis tools and techniques, and parameters that affect their performance

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Risk, Law Enforcement Engagement, Security Operations Group
jobs.description:
This position can be based at any Amazon Corporate Hub in EMEA.

You'll help build a global law enforcement engagement capability from scratch — designing the architecture that connects Amazon's security operations with policing agencies globally to disrupt organised crime at scale and create lasting purposeful symbiotic law enforcement relationships. As a Law Enforcement Engagement Leader for Rest of World, you will own the end-to-end law enforcement engagement strategy across EMEA, APAC, and MEA. You are accountable for building the relationship architecture, engagement frameworks, and intelligence-sharing models that turn connections into a structured, institutionally-owned network. You'll be part of a team securing cross-functional dependencies with Legal, Finance, and Global Security Operations Center (GSOC), and represent Amazon at the highest levels of international law enforcement.

There is no existing playbook and no inherited structure. You will help define the operating model, and you enable field teams to execute, maintaining local relationships, acting as the bridge to support.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the Law Enforcement Engagement strategy and operating model across EMEA, APAC, and MEA. Design and implement the three-tier relationship model (strategic, regional, local) across 30+ international jurisdictions, and build the Geographic Targeting Model to direct resources where loss, risk, and relationship gaps intersect. Deliver the priority-market heat map.
- Design the LE Partnership Registry, converting personal relationships into institutional, company-owned assets. Develop standardised engagement playbooks, Memorandum of Understanding frameworks, and SLA-driven inbound request processes tailored to civil-law and common-law jurisdictions. Build legally compliant information-sharing models co-designed with Legal, and establish bidirectional intelligence protocols with GSOC.
- Secure and maintain cross-functional dependencies across Legal, Finance, GSOC, Investigations, Public Policy, and ACS. Ensure formal deconfliction with Investigations across international markets.
- Help onboard and develop regional STLs across EMEA, APAC, and MEA. Set the operating rhythm from weekly stand-ups to quarterly business reviews. Mentor team members ensuring role clarity and career progression.
- Represent Amazon at the highest levels of international law enforcement — building executive relationships with INTERPOL, Europol, and national agencies, and leading engagement with industry bodies including TAPA, OPAL, and ASIS. Own governance oversight for ROW, ensuring alignment with WWOS-wide frameworks.

About the team
The LEE team sits within Amazon's Security Operations Group, building the institutional architecture that connects Amazon's security operations with law enforcement agencies across ROW 30+ international markets to disrupt organised crime targeting global logistics.

We believe relationships built in peacetime pay dividends in crisis. We deploy resources where data shows the greatest exposure, measure ourselves on outcomes — disrupted Mo's, asset recovery, threat disruption — not activity.

This is a team for builders. We are early-stage, high-ambition, and outcome-obsessed. You'll write the playbook, not inherit one.

- Experience in risk management, audit, legal, compliance or a related field including engaging with external stakeholders
- Experience in team management with 5 or more direct reports
- Experience implementing lean principles and process improvement in an operational environment
- Experience working within a global company, with multi-country responsibilities
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Experience in security service, loss prevention, asset protection, audit, investigations, law enforcement, risk management, data analytics, inventory control, quality assurance or a related field
- Experience creating and delivering written and oral communications for technical and non-technical audiences
- Experience leading the design, development and/or implementation of new business processes or programs
- Deep experience with public-private partnerships and information-sharing programmes across multiple jurisdictions
- Experience operating across international boundaries with an understanding of civil-law vs. common-law jurisdiction differences
Preferred qualifications:
- Knowledge of International Organization for Standardization (ISO), International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), or regulatory requirements or standards
- Experience with audit or risk program design, control environment process documentation, and control mapping
- Master's degree or equivalent

- Advanced project management skills, with a strong sense of accountability for outcomes
- Enjoyment of analytical tasks – working to create different scenarios based on alternative solutions

We're a collaborative group passionate about books and committed to making them accessible to everyone in Australia. Our team works across retail, vendor partnerships, and category strategy to continuously improve the customer experience. We value diverse perspectives and creative approaches to solving problems. As a Category Growth Manager, you'll be part of a supportive environment where your ideas matter, your contributions are visible, and you'll have the opportunity to influence how we serve our customers. jobs.description:
The Regional Procurement Manager (RPM) leads Amazon's OPEX Procurement at a regional level ensuring the continuous supply of essential non-inventory materials and services across the network. This role manages a geographically dispersed team serving approx 16 sites within East Midlands & South of UK, as per alignment of the new global model organisation. Team structure includes 4 Procurement Managers, who handle local procurement operations, and 5 Store Coordinators (SC), who manage on-site consumables for Operations. They support all end-to-end procurement operations for a diverse logistic network.

Home site location subject to discussion, but to be based within East Midlands & South of UK.

Key job responsibilities
Core responsibilities require expertise and responsibilities in 6 areas:

- Strategic operations management: The RPM develops and executes regional procurement strategies to drive network growth and operational excellence. This includes managing complex supply chain needs through supplier performance frameworks and demand planning coordination across facilities. This role requires a deep understanding of operational requirements that drive measurable business impact, while supporting SME coordination and enabling SPMs achieve stablished KPIs.

- People leadership: Leading a multi-site procurement team demands strong people management capabilities. The RPM builds and develops talent across geographically dispersed locations, ensuring team members have the tools and support needed to serve their respective sites effectively. This includes coaching SPMs and SC to maintain high performance standards and deliver consistent results across the network, while excelling in connection results.

- Stakeholder management: Success in this role depends on strong partnerships with senior site leadership and regional support functions. The RPM collaborates with key operational stakeholders through quarterly one-on-one meetings and maintains open communication channels throughout the year. They drive efficiency improvements and align procurement strategies with site objectives, deeply understanding operations processes and brilliant basics. Additional responsibilities include representing SPO in regional leadership forums and GPO workstreams, supporting SPMs in achieving site QBR targets, and managing strategic relationships with internal partners and external suppliers. The RPM also oversees high-complexity service disruptions, high-risk contracts, and senior stakeholder expectations.

- Cost optimization: The RPM develops direct reports capabilities to identify and capture sustainable savings aligned with company policies and reporting standards. RPMs ensure SPMs achieve regional targets through strategic procurement leadership, utilizing expertise in procurement strategy and category knowledge, while deploying company savings methodologies and value creation frameworks.

- Network optimization: RPMs standardize procurement processes and FC service activities while managing supply chain initiatives. They apply analytical tools for supply base optimization, supplier segmentation, and lead cross-functional cost projects. RPMs align global category strategies with local execution and contribute to SPO Global Initiatives through standardized practices across the FC network.

- Compliance and risk management: RPMs drive compliance and risk mitigation strategies. They ensure SPMs implement supplier governance frameworks, maintain procurement policy adherence, and manage supply chain risks. This includes oversight of due diligence processes (onboarding through Supplier Connect, TPS & others), contract compliance, and supplier adoption of required tools (including Avetta, Accurate or SR audit requirements).

jobs.description:
The Regional Procurement Manager (RPM) leads Amazon's site procurement operations (SPO) at a regional level ensuring the continuous supply of essential non-inventory materials and services across the network. This role manages a geographically dispersed team serving approx 18 sites within North of Germany, as per alignment of the new global model organisation. Team structure includes 5 plus Site Procurement Managers (SPM), who handle local procurement operations, and Store Coordinators (SC), who manage on-site consumables for Operations. They support all end-to-end procurement operations for a diverse logistic network with combined yearly sites spend of $250 MM.

Key job responsibilities
Core responsibilities require expertise and responsibilities in 6 areas:

Strategic operations management: The RPM develops and executes regional procurement strategies to drive network growth and operational excellence. This includes managing complex supply chain needs through supplier performance frameworks and demand planning coordination across facilities. This role requires a deep understanding of operational requirements that drive measurable business impact, while supporting SME coordination and enabling SPMs achieve stablished KPIs.

People leadership: Leading a multi-site procurement team demands strong people management capabilities. The RPM builds and develops talent across geographically dispersed locations, ensuring team members have the tools and support needed to serve their respective sites effectively. This includes coaching SPMs and SC to maintain high performance standards and deliver consistent results across the network, while excelling in connection results.

Stakeholder management: Success in this role depends on strong partnerships with senior site leadership and regional support functions. The RPM collaborates with key operational stakeholders through quarterly one-on-one meetings and maintains open communication channels throughout the year. They drive efficiency improvements and align procurement strategies with site objectives, deeply understanding operations processes and brilliant basics. Additional responsibilities include representing SPO in regional leadership forums and GPO workstreams, supporting SPMs in achieving site QBR targets, and managing strategic relationships with internal partners and external suppliers. The RPM also oversees high-complexity service disruptions, high-risk contracts, and senior stakeholder expectations.

Cost optimization: The RPM develops direct reports capabilities to identify and capture sustainable savings aligned with company policies and reporting standards. RPMs ensure SPMs achieve regional targets through strategic procurement leadership, utilizing expertise in procurement strategy and category knowledge, while deploying company savings methodologies and value creation frameworks.

Network optimization: RPMs standardize procurement processes and FC service activities while managing supply chain initiatives. They apply analytical tools for supply base optimization, supplier segmentation, and lead cross-functional cost projects. RPMs align global category strategies with local execution and contribute to SPO Global Initiatives through standardized practices across the FC network.

Compliance and risk management: RPMs drive compliance and risk mitigation strategies. They ensure SPMs implement supplier governance frameworks, maintain procurement policy adherence, and manage supply chain risks. jobs.description:
In pursuit of being Earth's Best Employer, our global Human Resources teams, known as People eXperience and Technology (PXT), drive business success by fostering a safe, inclusive, and innovative culture. The Senior HR Business Partner (Sr. HRBP) is a key strategic partner on the (North America Surface Transportation (NAST) PXT team, bringing expertise in leadership development, employee experience, culture, and change management. This role balances tactical excellence with strategic insight, leveraging both technology and human judgment to align local leadership, centralized support, and systems in delivering high-quality employee experiences.

The Sr. HRBP contributes to excellence in PXT service delivery through leadership and strategic insight. They support team development and process optimization while upholding high standards and risk management practices. Leveraging data and experience, they inform business decisions and help implement scalable solutions. Their influence extends across the organization, collaborating with leaders to advance key initiatives and deliver solutions that balance immediate needs with long-term objectives.

You will be expected to work onsite at an Amazon facility.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead and develop a diverse team of HR professionals, coaching them to elevate beyond tactical execution to become strategic partners who proactively identify and mitigate organizational risks while delivering exceptional service.

- Drive a culture of proactive risk identification and mitigation by establishing early warning systems, leveraging data insights, and building strong partnerships across functions. Guide your team in developing sound judgment to spot emerging people-related risks before they impact the business.

- Shape the strategic vision for employee experience and organizational health. Challenge status quo thinking and drive innovation in HR practices while ensuring sustainable execution. Enable your team to move beyond immediate problem-solving to address systemic issues and opportunities.

- Partner with business leadership to develop and execute integrated talent strategies that address both current needs and future capability requirements. Coach leaders on effective talent development while building a strong succession pipeline within your own HR organization. Anticipate future talent needs and evolving workforce dynamics to future-proof both operations and HR.

- Lead your team in effective use of analytics and AI tools to uncover hidden patterns, predict emerging risks, and drive data-informed decision making. Translate complex insights into compelling narratives that influence senior stakeholders and drive organizational change.

- Set clear goals for culture transformation with business leaders. Design and implement comprehensive strategies to systematically strengthen organizational health, talent capabilities, and leadership effectiveness. Champion initiatives that measurably enhance diversity, equity and inclusion.

- Drive strategic adoption of HR technology to enable both efficiency and excellence in service delivery. Guide your team to leverage automation while preserving high-touch support for sensitive employee matters requiring human judgment and empathy.

A day in the life
A typical day involves balancing strategic insight with tactical execution. You'll provide expertise in employee relations, coach leaders through performance and development matters, and drive HR functional excellence. Operating with autonomy, you'll partner with leaders at multiple levels to develop forward-looking strategies focused on employee experience and operational objectives.

Through data analytics and AI-enabled tools, you'll identify trends and opportunities while maintaining the human connections essential for building trust. You'll support critical HR processes such as investigations and talent management while leveraging technology to enhance service delivery and decision-making, knowing when automation creates efficiency and when personal interaction remains crucial.

Success in this role comes from effectively enabling strong people leadership, influencing at scale, and addressing root causes of systemic issues. Through a combination of data-driven insights and strategic partnerships, you'll help create and maintain a workplace culture where employees feel valued, supported, and empowered to perform at their best.

Our teams play a critical role in ensuring the smooth and efficient operations of Amazon's transportation network as well as innovating on industry leading technology programs.

- Experience using data and high-judgement to drive business decisions
- Experience supporting and/or leading employee-focused processes such as onboarding, benefits, investigations, training and/or talent management

- Experience supporting large employee populations in manufacturing, retail, distribution, or similar operational environments
- Knowledge of employment law, employee relations, and HR compliance requirements
- Experience resolving sensitive employee relations issues
- Experience partnering with, coaching, and guiding senior leaders as a strategic HR business partner

jobs.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services provides a highly reliable, scalable, and low-cost cloud platform that powers thousands of businesses in over 190 countries. AWS’ Infrastructure Supply Chain & Procurement organization works to deliver solutions to source, build and maintain our socially responsible data center supply chains. We are a team of highly-motivated, engaged, and responsive professionals who enable the core sustainable infrastructure of AWS. Come join our team and be a part of history as we deliver results for the largest cloud services company on Earth!

The IPS Procurement Category Management Org is responsible for the procurement of all third party provided services required for the operation of our Data Center infrastructure globally, including Colo and Edge facilities for externally delivered services not provided by the facility owner. The team is responsible for the identification, on boarding and performance management of suppliers as well as developing category strategies, conducting competitive tendering processes, supplier negotiations and the preparation of associated Work Orders.

The team is structured into three regions, each led by a regional manager, with each regional team composed of category managers with responsibility for the management of specific areas of spend within the region and a cohort of procurement specialists who support the category managers. The category management approach facilitates a strategic approach to procurement by facilitating in depth market analysis coupled with a cross functional approach to identify supplier and associated contracting options which are focused on meeting the particular needs of the business. Category management moves beyond traditional transactional based purchasing negotiations to provide a strategic approach to longer term, sustainable cost reductions, reducing risk and increasing resiliency in the supply base and facilitating innovation from within the supply base that the business can leverage.
While cost reduction will always be a key focus of the team, the principle cynosure of the team is the delivery of services that are keenly focused on increasing reliability and supporting enhanced availability through robust relationships which support continuity of operations. As service and quality levels can vary greatly, principally based on the skill set within a supplier local organization, the regional structure facilitates tailoring of category strategies to meet local market considerations and closely monitor supplier performance at the local level.

Key job responsibilities
The ideal candidate thinks long term, drives multiple initiatives, and communicates appropriately and influences customers and suppliers at all levels. You must be collaborative, but also work with significant autonomy. To be successful in this role you must be highly analytical; think strategically and globally; have a sense of urgency to meet customer timelines; exhibit curiosity and learning drive; succeed in a fast-paced environment; engage and influence key stakeholders; and have a high level of customer focus and business judgement. Also, you must have a demonstrated track record of managing multiple projects and driving them to completion to meet business objectives. It will be critical to embrace and model Amazon’s Leadership Principles and have an entrepreneurial spirit with a “get it done” mentality.

•Manage a complex category within the Maintenance, Repair, and Operation (MRO) and Facility Management domains.

•Achieve cost savings through bidding and negotiations, drive collaboration to achieve long term value delivery.

•Obtain market intelligence, analyze category data and metrics to drive Procurement category strategies.

•Understand trends in customers’ needs and concerns, across categories and regions, to influence customers’ priorities.

•Lead supplier selection process across multiple sub-categories, internal teams, and regions, and create longer-term supplier selection strategies for management.

•Ensure you are knowledgeable about the supply market, new innovations and supplier capabilities, technically and geographically.

•Ensure you are knowledgeable about sustainability, diversity, in-country value and have experience developing category strategies to incorporate same.

•Develop mechanisms and metrics to track supplier performance related to delivery, quality, and cost.

•Create supplier scorecards to measure and track supplier performance.

•Lead business reviews to discuss best practices and issues and to ultimately improve supplier performance and strengthen business partnerships.

•Innovate within the procurement space, automating and/or improving tools or processes to better support the Procurement Lifecycle.

•Provide support throughout the contracting process, as well as SRM and management of contracts post-execution.

Travel domestic and international as required.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

jobs.title: Audit & Compliance Manager, Transportation Risk and Compliance (TRC)
jobs.description:
Amazon’s Transportation Risk & Compliance (TRC) team identifies and mitigates risk in a rapidly growing and complex, global environment. To support the business, our primary mission is to perform independent and objective, risk-based assessments of Amazon business partners’ activities and related controls with the goal of improving operations, compliance, risk management, and overall success of the program. We provide Audit & Monitoring (A&M) support of high-risk transportation risk topics to drive compliance across the transportation programs and influence business controls.

We are seeking an experienced professional in audit, risk, controls, governance and program management, to join our Australia (AU) TRC Last Mile (LM) Field Operations (FO) team, to lead and execute Audit & Monitoring (A&M) across AU LM transportation programs. In this role, you will work closely with Amazon's AU LM transportation businesses to plan, scope, and execute audits to verify carrier partners are meeting legal and contractual obligations relating to business practices, driver / provider eligibility, and safety standards. You will be expected to apply risk and control concepts to new and existing business models, clearly and concisely communicate identified findings to carrier partners, and internally report audit results in a timely and effective manner. You will provide carriers with consultative support to identify opportunities for improvement, develop corrective action plans to address audit defects, and manage those remediation plans to closure. You will also work collaboratively with the operations, business, safety, legal, public policy, finance, and tech teams to implement world-class, customer-centric, compliance and risk management solutions. To bring in best practices and learning, you’ll also work with and learn from colleagues globally.

This is a small but growing team, meaning you'll play an instrumental role in developing the function, defining and developing the value that we offer to our business partners, and how we achieve strategic goals, in a business which continues to grow rapidly.

This role can be based in Sydney NSW or Melbourne VIC.

Key job responsibilities
Transport is a wide discipline, and you will have an opportunity to learn about a range of disciplines, such as employment law, safety, driver licensing, etc, in addition to performing periodic site visits.

• Manage and oversee end-to-end execution A&M programs to determine if third-party transportation partners are compliant with contractual and regulatory requirements.
• Liaise with Global Quality team to ensure alignment to global audit quality standards and metrics
• Manage A&M findings, ensuring closure, or enforcement actions if they are not closed on time.
• Collate and provide regular reporting of A&M metrics for local and global reporting
• Perform deep dives of processes to identify risks, controls, and gaps, and use that information to influence business
• Independently manage the yearly audit plan, and own the end-to-end audit lifecycle
• Define A&M program scope and tests for new LM programs engaging with key stakeholders including business, operations, legal, public policy, and other compliance teams.
• Manage relationships with cross functional stakeholders internal and external to Amazon
• Scale audits through automation and AI.
• Advise the business on risk and compliance issues for new transportation initiatives, processes, risks and controls and building solutions despite ambiguity.
• Deliver quality, business-oriented reports that are written with practical, actionable, and value-added recommendations

A day in the life
Audit & Compliance Managers engage with Carrier Partners, plan, scope, execute, and report on the audit outcomes. The individual provides consultative support and guidance on corrective actions to Carrier Partners and verifies remediation. Audit & Compliance Managers will also consult with business, legal, and tech teams to develop gap remediation strategies and the build-out of sustainable and systematic solutions. The individual will work effectively in a team environment and, as individual contributors, be able to work remotely and effectively review the work of other remote team members.

About the team
Transportation Risk and Compliance (TRC) is the voice of risk and compliance for Amazon’s transportation businesses across 24+ countries. We proactively identify and manage risks through risk mitigation strategies and provide assurance that Amazon and our carrier partners comply with the highest transportation and legal standards (including legislative, regulatory, and contractual). Anchored by sound subject matter expertise, processes, and growing technology solutions, our TRC leaders improve public safety and enable business growth as we work diligently to serve our customers.
Basic qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent experience)
- 3+ years of experience in auditing, risk management, compliance, program management, or quality management systems
- 3+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience establishing successful partnerships with internal and external teams to execute tactical initiatives or equivalent
- Experience of interacting regularly and directly with senior executives.
- Ability to independently manage a project and demonstrate sound judgment even in ambiguous situations
- Ability to turn complex compliance requirements into scalable processes
Preferred qualifications:
- Professional auditing qualification, or similar risk or compliance credentials
- Experience with SQL and Excel
- Knowledge of retail food code and regulations governing grocery retail at local, state, and federal levels
- Experience in accounting management in Big Four with Fortune 500 clients, or experience in tax, finance or a related analytical field
- Knowledge of payroll and the modern awards system, and third-party risk management
- Experience working in the operations, transportation, and logistics sectors.

jobs.title: Director, Network Infrastructure Sourcing & Procurement, Networking and Server Silicon
jobs.description:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is looking for an experienced senior leader to serve as Director of Network Infrastructure Sourcing and Procurement. This role owns the end-to-end sourcing strategy for the components that connect every server in every AWS data center to the network, one of the fastest-growing and most technically complex portfolios in the company.
You will lead a global organization responsible for the procurement of networking ASICs, optical transceivers, lasers, optical fiber cable, and OEM networking equipment. This portfolio is experiencing extraordinary growth driven by AI and machine learning infrastructure expansion, with spend scaling multiple times over the next two years.
In this role, you will build and lead a team of senior sourcing and supply chain leaders while owning executive relationships with CEOs and senior leaders at the world's leading semiconductor, photonics, and fiber optic companies. You will develop multi-year sourcing strategies that secure supply, reduce total cost of ownership, mitigate geopolitical risk, and position AWS to meet its growth targets.
You will work at the intersection of latest networking technology and global supply chain operations. This requires deep technical curiosity and the ability to translate complex technology roadmaps into clear commercial strategies.
The ideal candidate is a proven executive leader who combines large-scale technical supply chain expertise with the ability to build high-performing organizations, influence at the highest levels, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. They bring a track record of defining and executing category strategies at scale, driving complex negotiations, building deep supplier partnerships, and creating scalable processes that deliver continuous improvement.
This Director will be a key member of the AWS Supply Chain senior leadership team. You will be responsible for fostering an inclusive, high-performance culture, developing the next generation of leaders, and continuously raising the talent bar across the organization.

Key job responsibilities
• Define and execute category sourcing strategies across networking silicon, optical components, fiber infrastructure, and switching platforms, aligned with the AWS multi-year growth and technology roadmap.
• Build, develop, and lead a high-performing global organization spanning multiple geographies, with strong leadership depth and succession planning across the team.
• Own executive-level relationships with strategic suppliers, influencing their technology investments, capacity allocation, and product roadmaps to serve long-term AWS interests.
• Negotiate complex commercial agreements including long-term supply agreements, capacity reservations, and strategic investment structures at significant scale.
• Provide regular updates to VP-level leadership on supply strategy, risk posture, and critical commercial decisions requiring approval.
• Develop supply diversification and risk mitigation strategies addressing geopolitical exposure, single-source dependencies, and technology transition risks.
• Drive cross-functional alignment with Hardware Engineering, Manufacturing Design Engineering, Finance, Legal, and Capacity Delivery organizations.
• Identify and close critical supply gaps across a portfolio growing at exceptional rates.
• Create scalable mechanisms and data-driven decision frameworks to support rapid portfolio growth.
• Build an inclusive, high-performance team culture while developing the next generation of supply chain leaders.

A day in the life
This Director leads the sourcing strategy for all networking components (ASICs, optical transceivers, lasers, fiber cable, OEM equipment). Day to day includes negotiating multi-billion dollar supplier agreements, qualifying next generation silicon and photonics, managing geopolitical supply risks, and briefing VP leadership on critical decisions. You work across Engineering, Finance, Legal, and Capacity Delivery teams. Your internal customers are data center teams who need components delivered on time so servers can connect to the network and generate revenue. The core problem: a portfolio growing 7x in two years where supply must be secured 12 to 18 months in advance or it is gone.

- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, or a related field
- 10+ years of people leadership, or 10+ years of senior leadership experience
- 6+ years of multi-million dollar contract negotiation experience
- Experience working with, presenting to, and negotiating with C-level executives, IT, lines of business, procurement, finance, legal and internal stakeholders for sizeable commercial/enterprise deals
- Experience shaping business strategy for technical products or services for large enterprises or partners
- Experience in written and verbal communication skills to communicate with technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership
Preferred qualifications:

- 6+ years of developing diverse supplier strategies and executing on sourcing activities experience
- Experience taking a leading role in building complex software or computing infrastructure that has been successfully delivered to customers
- Experience working in a fast-paced, rapidly changing operations environment
- Experience in supply chain security, including management of third-party logistics providers, law enforcement, loss prevention, risk management, investigations or a similar field

- Experience demonstrating strong analytical abilities and confidence in the use of data

This role is for a Customer Success Manager (CSM) on the Zappos FBA Preferred Partnerships team. The position is a new headcount designed to serve as a dedicated strategic growth partner for assigned footwear brands within our Preferred Partnership Program (PPP).

The CSM will operate as the primary relationship owner and trusted advisor for their brand portfolio, personally engaging with vendor stakeholders to develop trust, influence strategic decisions, and align brand goals with Amazon growth opportunities. This role requires navigating complex multi-stakeholder environments, influencing without authority across internal teams (Buying & Planning, Supply Chain, Advertising), and building durable partnerships through consistent personal engagement, transparent communication, and accountable follow-through.

This role is highly visible and requires a balance of tactical execution and strategic relationship management. Success in this role means earning the trust of brand partners through reliable personal engagement, driving selection growth through coordinated investment, and strengthening the scalability of the PPP through accountable partnership ownership.

Key job responsibilities
Partnership Ownership & Relationship Management: Serve as the dedicated point of contact for assigned footwear brands, building trusted advisory relationships through regular touchpoints, proactive communication, and responsive issue resolution. Engage with brand stakeholders to understand their business objectives and translate them into actionable growth strategies. Maintain defined response SLAs and conduct quarterly Partnership Health Reviews.

Strategic Growth & Business Planning: Develop Joint Business Plans with buyers and vendors to align growth priorities and partnership commitments. Create one-page Brand Growth Briefs covering demand signals, whitespace opportunities, and exclusivity strategies. Attend market appointments to influence buy depth and surface growth opportunities with brand decision-makers.

Demand Acceleration & Investment Coordination: Coordinate Sponsored Ads, merchandising, promotions, and catalog optimization to drive traffic, conversion, and organic rank growth. Manage deal mechanics and identify cost-engineered opportunities for event eligibility.

Controlled Distribution & Customer Experience: Monitor seller fragmentation, Featured Offer ownership, and pricing consistency. Coordinate Brand Store, A+ Content, and catalog updates to improve listing quality and customer trust.

Reporting & Operational Excellence: Deliver monthly Brand Exposure Reports and weekly business recaps. Build scalable reporting and process improvements to support program growth.

A day in the life
Your day might start reviewing Featured Offer trends and seller fragmentation for a Priority Partner, then shift to coordinating a Sponsored Ads campaign launch with the media team. Mid-morning, you're on a call with a brand stakeholder discussing their quarterly growth plan. After lunch, you're preparing a one-page exclusivity brief for an upcoming market appointment, then submitting deal mechanics for a high-velocity event. You close the day delivering a vendor digest and flagging pricing risks to the buying team. No two days look the same, but every day connects brand strategy to measurable Amazon outcomes.

The Preferred Partnerships Program (PPP) is a growth and distribution management team within Zappos FBA team. We serve as strategic partners to premium footwear brands, helping them grow on Amazon through controlled distribution, coordinated advertising investment, and accountable ownership. Our Customer Success Managers work alongside Buying & Planning to accelerate demand, expand exclusivity, optimize Featured Offer performance, and improve the customer experience. We manage a tiered portfolio of Priority, Growth, and Emerging partners, scaling investment and support based on each brand's strategic value and commitment level.

- Proven ability to build trusted advisory relationships with external stakeholders
- Track record driving measurable partner outcomes (revenue growth, operational improvements, or adoption)

jobs.description:
At Amazon, our vision is to be Earth's most customer-centric company. Our passion for invention leads us to pioneer and globalize new businesses and customer offerings daily. As we rapidly become the world’s largest consumer of corporate services in many categories, the Corporate Procurement team is fueling our explosive growth by identifying innovative sourcing strategies and negotiating sustainable, long-term partnerships.

Amazon is seeking a Strategic Sourcing Manager to join the Corporate Procurement team. The role is based in Tokyo, Japan. This role serves in a pivotal role, leading strategic sourcing engagements across a wide range of business units to enable new business initiatives to launch and scale rapidly. Spend categories under management include Marketing, Professional Services, HR, Travel, Perm & Temp Labor, Architecture, Construction, and Property/Facilities. Key leadership traits required include the ability to influence and form strong partnerships with business leaders, and operational excellence in managing multiple complex and competing priorities simultaneously.

Our team are expert practitioners in the tools for creating competitive environments, and have a strong bias for decision-making rooted in data and analytics. We routinely influence C-level vendor relationships by advising senior Amazon leaders across multiple stakeholder groups on the direction of sourcing projects in support of business unit and corporate goals. If you are looking for a new challenge in a fast-paced, innovative company, come make history with Amazon’s Corporate Procurement department.

• Establishing strong relationships with internal business stakeholders; building a strong understanding of strategic business direction, requirements and priorities across assigned suppliers and/or spend categories.
• Developing global sourcing strategies to deliver against business objectives for internal clients.
• Evaluating supplier core competencies and competitive positioning using industry cost models and bench-marking analysis.
• Managing the fundamentals of sourcing and supplier engagement activities including RFx, spend pattern analysis, contract analysis, bid evaluation, negotiations, and supplier consolidation.
• Identifying sourcing opportunities by leveraging spend analysis tools and engage with stakeholders to consolidate requirements over categories, suppliers and geographies.
• Work with business and finance leaders to identify and drive savings and controllership improvements, focusing on total cost of ownership.

jobs.description:
In pursuit of being Earth's Best Employer, our global Human Resources teams, known as People eXperience and Technology (PXT), drive business success by fostering a safe, inclusive, and innovative culture. The HR Business Partner provides HR generalist support to a large population of hourly employees and business leaders, bringing expertise in leadership development, employee experience, and operational excellence.

In this role, you will partner with business leaders to deliver HR initiatives focused on talent management, employee engagement, and internal customer service. Success requires leveraging data-driven insights and understanding the importance of HR metrics to drive business impact. You may also lead a team of entry-level HR employees and own projects that enhance the employee experience.

The HR Business Partner balances strategic and tactical responsibilities, driving organizational success through partnership with leaders. They execute core PXT processes while providing guidance on talent processes, performance management, and cultural initiatives. By building trust and influence through sound business acumen, they manage increasingly complex issues and deliver solutions that enhance both employee experience and business outcomes.

You will be expected to work onsite at an Amazon facility.

Key job responsibilities
- Improve site effectiveness by identifying systemic patterns, addressing root causes, and making high-judgment decisions that align with policy intent while minimizing risk. Establish and implement mechanisms that ensure consistent, fair application of policies while maintaining compliance with evolving regulations.

- Use data analytics to identify emerging trends, predict future challenges, and implement proactive solutions at the site level. Turn insights into practical initiatives that drive measurable improvements in employee experience and business performance.

- Execute and monitor employee engagement strategies and recognition programs. Maintain meaningful floor presence to gather insights, identify early signs of disengagement, and partner with leaders to drive targeted improvements.

- Coach Business Leaders on effective people management practices, including performance feedback, team development, and complex employee relations matters. Support leaders in building inclusive, high-performing teams.

- Partner with leaders to ensure equitable talent practices across selection, development, and advancement decisions. Champion initiatives that create an inclusive environment where all employees can thrive.

- Drive adoption of HR technology solutions, AI, and self-service tools, ensuring effective utilization while maintaining focus on high-touch service delivery in critical moments. Identify opportunities to enhance user experience and process efficiency.

A day in the life
Your day will be a dynamic blend of strategic thinking and data-driven decision-making. You'll focus on driving organizational effectiveness and employee engagement, leveraging advanced analytics and AI-enabled tools to identify trends, anticipate business needs, and develop solutions that enhance workplace experience and deliver measurable results.

From coaching leadership teams on workforce and talent management to driving HR process excellence, you'll collaborate with business leaders to develop forward-looking strategies focused on operational objectives and team effectiveness. You'll build strong partnerships across all levels of the organization while contributing to meaningful workplace improvements.

Success in this role comes from your ability to navigate organizational dynamics, lead change initiatives, and make high-judgment decisions in ambiguous situations. Through a combination of business acumen, data-driven insights, and strategic partnerships, you'll help create a workplace culture where employees feel valued and empowered, while driving long-term organizational success and adaptability in a rapidly evolving business landscape.

Grocery Fulfillment Centers (GFC) continuously aims to build a best-in-class grocery experience for our customers where Amazon is the first choice for selection, value, and convenience—whether shopping in store or online. The GFC PXT team helps support the ever-changing, exciting GFC businesses within Amazon’s specialty network and retail stores across the globe. However, we all have a common goal - obsessing over our customers. Join our team and see what’s in store next for GFC PXT!

- Experience supporting and/or leading employee-focused processes such as onboarding, benefits, investigations, training and/or talent management

- Experience supporting operational environments (manufacturing, distribution, or similar)
